subject.title: [Feature]: Intelligent Model Fallback with Wildcard/Auto Selection

question: Which public provider-family fallback contract should OpenClaw support for model failover: implicit provider wildcard/auto selection, explicit grouped fallback families, a narrower catalog-derived opt-in, or none for now?
rationale: This changes public model config, provider/auth routing, and operator cost/quality expectations; code inspection shows no existing canonical contract to extend mechanically.

options.title: Adopt explicit grouped fallbacks
options.body: Add a `fallbackFamilies`-style explicit ordered contract so operators control family boundaries without relying on implicit provider catalog selection.

options.title: Adopt provider auto/wildcard
options.body: Add `provider/auto` or `provider/*` failover semantics backed by provider catalog/default-model rules, accepting more automatic behavior and more policy surface.

options.title: Limit to catalog-derived fallback or defer
options.body: Treat PR #60922 or existing flat `fallbacks` as the supported path for now and leave wildcard/grouped semantics out of core until the design is clearer.

recommendation.title: Adopt explicit grouped fallbacks
recommendation.body: Add a `fallbackFamilies`-style explicit ordered contract so operators control family boundaries without relying on implicit provider catalog selection.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal spans agent runtime, model fallback behavior, and shared model config schema surfaces.
